description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern feast, featuring succulent lamb slow roasted to perfection until it falls off the bone. This celebratory dish is often served atop fragrant spiced rice, garnished with toasted nuts, offering a symphony of textures and aromas. It is the centerpiece of any special occasion, promising an unforgettable dining experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb Marinade
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine 1/4 cup olive oil, 6 minced garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 tablespoons Seven Spice, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom, 1 teaspoon black pepper, and 2 teaspoons salt. Mix well to form a paste.

instructions.title: Marinate and Prepare Lamb for Roasting
instructions.text: Pat the lamb leg dry with paper towels. Make several deep incisions all over the lamb with a sharp knife. Rub the spice paste generously into the lamb, ensuring it gets into the incisions. Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan with the quartered onion and bay leaves. Pour 2 cups of water or lamb stock into the bottom of the pan. Cover the pan tightly with foil.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 325F (160C). Roast the covered lamb for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until it is very tender and easily falls off the bone. For the last 30 minutes of cooking, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown slightly and develop a crust. Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20 minutes before shredding. Reserve the flavorful pan juices.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice Base
instructions.text: While the lamb rests, begin preparing the rice. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in 3 minced garlic cloves and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add 1 tablespoon Seven Spice, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the spices are aromatic.

instructions.title: Cook the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot and stir to coat each grain evenly with the spices. Pour in 5 cups of chicken or lamb stock. If using, add the optional frozen peas and diced carrots. Bring the mixture to a boil, then immediately reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing gently with a fork.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve the Ouzi
instructions.text: Carefully shred the slow-roasted lamb from the bone using two forks. Gently mix some of the reserved pan juices into the shredded lamb to keep it moist and infuse more flavor. Arrange the fragrant spiced Ouzi rice on a large serving platter. Generously top the rice with the tender shredded lamb. Garnish with the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot as a magnificent center-piece.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, prepare the lamb marinade a day in advance and let the lamb marinate in the refrigerator overnight. This allows the spices to deeply penetrate the meat for maximum taste.
Authentic Ouzi often includes ground beef or lamb mixed into the rice. You can brown 1/2 lb of ground meat with the onions before adding the rice for a richer, more traditional dish.

Any leftover lamb and rice can be stored separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave, adding a splash of stock to the rice if it seems dry to maintain moisture.
article:
**Experience the Grandeur of Middle Eastern Feasts: Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi**

Imagine a centerpiece dish so magnificent, so aromatic, and so utterly delicious that it instantly transports you to the heart of a vibrant Middle Eastern celebration. That dish is Lamb Ouzi, a culinary masterpiece revered for its tender, falling-off-the-bone lamb and its exquisitely spiced rice, often studded with nuts and dried fruits. While traditionally a whole roasted lamb, this article focuses on capturing the essence of this grand feast using a large cut of lamb, slow-roasted to perfection, making it achievable for your next special gathering. Prepare to impress your guests and delight your senses with this unforgettable Middle Eastern dinner recipe.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozi" or "Ghozi," is a highly celebrated dish across the Levant and other parts of the Middle East. It’s more than just a meal; it's a symbol of hospitality, generosity, and festivity. At its core, Lamb Ouzi consists of slow-cooked, incredibly tender lamb – typically a whole lamb or a large cut like a leg or shoulder – served atop or alongside a rich, aromatic rice pilaf. The rice itself is often a star, infused with a blend of warming spices like allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, and black pepper, and generously mixed with toasted nuts (almonds, pine nuts, pistachios) and sometimes sweet dried fruits like raisins or apricots. The slow roasting process allows the lamb to become exceptionally succulent, absorbing all the wonderful flavors from its marinade and developing a beautiful, golden-brown crust.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create this show-stopping Lamb Ouzi, you’ll need a combination of high-quality ingredients that contribute to its distinctive flavor profile.

**For the Lamb:**
*   1 large lamb leg or shoulder (4-6 lbs/1.8-2.7 kg), bone-in or boneless
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   4-6 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tbsp ground allspice
*   1 tbsp ground cinnamon
*   1 tsp ground cardamom
*   1 tsp black pepper
*   1 tsp salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 tsp ground turmeric (optional, for color)
*   Juice of 1 lemon
*   1 cup chicken or lamb broth (for basting)

**For the Ouzi Rice:**
*   2 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   3 tbsp olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   4 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 tbsp ground allspice
*   1 tsp ground cinnamon
*   1/2 tsp ground cardamom
*   1/2 tsp black pepper
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, for a hint of heat)
*   4 cups chicken or lamb broth
*   1/2 cup slivered almonds, toasted
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1/4 cup golden raisins (optional)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh parsley or mint, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Preparing this dish requires patience, but the steps are straightforward and rewarding.

1.  **Marinate the Lamb:** Pat the lamb dry. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper, salt, turmeric (if using), and lemon juice to form a paste. Rub this paste generously all over the lamb. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate.
2.  **Preheat Oven & Prepare for Roasting:** Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Remove the lamb from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature for about 30-60 minutes.
3.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Place the lamb in the roasting pan. Add 1 cup of broth to the bottom of the pan. Cover the pan tightly with foil. Roast for 3-4 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender. The exact time will depend on the size and cut of your lamb. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil and increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. The internal temperature should reach 145°F (63°C) for medium-rare, 160°F (71°C) for medium, or 170°F (77°C) for well-done.
4.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This is crucial for juicy, tender meat.
5.  **Prepare the Ouzi Rice:** While the lamb is resting, start the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
6.  **Add Spices and Rice:** Stir in allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper, turmeric, and cayenne (if using). Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Add the rinsed basmati rice and stir to coat every grain with the spiced oil.
7.  **Cook the Rice:** Pour in the broth and add salt to taste. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
8.  **Finish the Rice:** Once cooked, remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5-10 minutes. Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Stir in the toasted almonds, pine nuts, and golden raisins (if using).

## Tips for Perfect Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving an exquisite Lamb Ouzi is all about attention to detail:

*   **Quality Lamb:** Start with a good quality cut of lamb. Bone-in cuts often yield more flavor and stay moister.
*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the lamb marinates, the deeper the flavor will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Low and Slow:** The secret to truly tender lamb is slow roasting at a low temperature. This breaks down connective tissues without drying out the meat.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** Always allow the lamb to rest after roasting. This redistributes the juices, resulting in a more tender and flavorful outcome.
*   **Toast Your Nuts:** Toasting almonds and pine nuts brings out their natural oils and enhances their flavor and aroma, adding a wonderful textural contrast to the rice.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks relatively quickly. Overcooking can make it mushy. Follow the liquid-to-rice ratio and cooking times carefully.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but a few accompaniments can elevate the experience:

*   **Garnish:** Generously sprinkle the finished dish with fresh chopped parsley or mint for a burst of color and freshness. A final scattering of extra toasted nuts is also a lovely touch.
*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A cooling yogurt-based sauce like Labneh (strained yogurt) or a simple cucumber-mint tzatziki provides a refreshing counterpoint to the rich lamb and spiced rice.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Light, crisp salads such as Fattoush (bread salad) or Tabbouleh (parsley and bulgur salad) offer brightness and acidity that cut through the richness of the main dish.
*   **Pickles and Olives:** A platter of assorted Middle Eastern pickles and olives adds tangy notes and a delightful crunch.
*   **Flatbread:** Warm pita bread or other Middle Eastern flatbreads are perfect for scooping up every last bit of the delicious rice and lamb.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Lamb Ouzi is magnificent, feel free to experiment:

*   **Lamb Cuts:** If a whole leg or shoulder is too large, you can use lamb shanks or even smaller lamb chops. Adjust roasting times accordingly.
*   **Rice Additions:** For a heartier rice, consider adding a handful of cooked brown lentils or chickpeas.
*   **Vegetables:** Root vegetables like carrots, potatoes, or sweet potatoes can be roasted alongside the lamb for an all-in-one meal.
*   **Nut & Fruit Mix-ins:** Experiment with different nuts like pistachios or walnuts, and other dried fruits such as dried cranberries or chopped dried apricots.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Customize the spice blend to your preference. A touch of sumac can add a lovely tang.

## Storage and Reheating Tips

Proper storage ensures you can enjoy your Lamb Ouzi leftovers for days.

*   **Refrigeration:** Store leftover lamb and rice separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** Both the cooked lamb and the rice freeze well. Freeze in airtight, freezer-safe containers for up to 2-3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating Lamb:** Gently reheat the lamb in the oven at 300°F (150°C), covered with foil, until warmed through. A splash of broth can help keep it moist.
*   **Reheating Rice:** Reheat the rice on the stovetop with a tablespoon or two of water or broth, covered, over low heat, stirring occasionally. Alternatively, microwave with a damp paper towel over it.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Can I prepare Lamb Ouzi ahead of time?**
A: Yes! The lamb can be marinated overnight. The rice can be cooked a day in advance and gently reheated. This makes it perfect for entertaining.

**Q: What if I don't have a whole lamb or a large leg?**
A: You can absolutely make a delicious Lamb Ouzi with smaller cuts like lamb shanks, shoulder chops, or even boneless lamb stew meat. Adjust cooking times accordingly.

**Q: Is Lamb Ouzi spicy?**
A: Traditional Lamb Ouzi is rich in warming spices like allspice, cinnamon, and cardamom, but it's generally not "hot" spicy. The cayenne pepper in the recipe is optional for those who prefer a little kick.

**Q: How do I prevent the lamb from drying out during slow roasting?**
A: Key strategies include thorough marination, roasting at a low temperature, keeping the roasting pan covered tightly with foil for most of the cooking time, and basting occasionally. Resting the lamb after cooking is also crucial for moisture retention.

**Q: Can I use brown rice instead of basmati?**
A: While basmati is traditional, you can use brown rice. However, it will require a longer cooking time and potentially more liquid. Adjust accordingly based on package instructions.

Embrace the joy of slow cooking and the rich tapestry of Middle Eastern flavors with this incredible Lamb Ouzi. It’s a dish that promises not just a meal, but an experience – one that celebrates tradition, flavor, and the warmth of shared moments. Enjoy bringing this magnificent feast to your own table!
